payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into how systems recover from noisy entity linking by employing various strategies such as query structure ranking, filtering out erroneous links, and leveraging training data to improve performance.

claims.text: SubQG ranks query structures first and filters out many erroneous linking results through checks, allowing it to still generate correct answers in 85% of cases despite noise.
The approach utilizes multiple networks to learn predictors for different query substructures, which helps maintain stable performance even with noisy linking results.
Merging query substructures can improve recall, especially when training data is limited, thus aiding recovery from noisy linking.
